change: Compile recurrent loss, gradients, Adam and finite checks together; dynamically select the unchanged balanced training schedule. No learning recipe or acceptance gate changes.

tests.scope: Existing buoyancy training tests plus compiled/eager schedule/checkpoint parity and gradient/parameter nonfinite regressions; frozen production lock on non-DGX CPU.

interpretation: Both completed comparisons preserve all 256 updates, the selected update, original reference/FD/restart gates, and near-identical float32 loss histories/parameters. This is an execution optimization, not an accuracy improvement.
JAX shows a substantial paired training reduction. The first Phi profile showed a 1.22% regression; this negative result is deliberately retained.

The counterbalanced Phi repeat with node-local logs shows a 15.09% training reduction. Both order and logging changed, so the difference between Phi trials is not proof that filesystem logging alone caused the earlier result.
First-call work is included, but shared persistent executable caches were enabled. No claim of isolated cold compilation or cold end-to-end CI speedup.
Reference generation and initial admission are shared preparation, unchanged by this patch. Whole CI also includes image/setup/plotting costs not measured by the fit comparison.
Sampled process RSS is distinct from Slurm whole-allocation MaxRSS. Both measures are retained; no claim that the whole job fits within the smaller sampled fit-phase RSS.

preserved_setup_failure.failure: Server configured with cuda-only backend; Phi DLPack host conversion required CPU backend too. Retried with cuda,cpu while asserting default GPU; CPU client unchanged. Not a numerical training failure.

benchmark_ci_label: Not enabled or dispatched by this work
large_raw_artifacts: No NPZ arrays, raw HTTP logs, or source tar archives copied to this artifact folder; hashes and cluster locations retained.
